html:
NAFTA, the North American Free Trade Agreement, joined Canada, the United States and Mexico in one of the world's largest free trade areas. It ran from 1 January 1994 until 2020.

It built on a free trade deal between Canada and the United States of 1988. Leaders of the three countries, among them Mexico's Carlos Salinas, signed it in 1992, and Bill Clinton pushed it through Congress the next year. It removed most tariffs between the three countries over fifteen years.

  • Trade among the three grew several times over.
  • Car makers built supply chains that crossed the borders many times.
  • Factories in northern Mexico, the maquiladoras, boomed.
  • Small Mexican corn farmers struggled against cheap US maize.

On the day it began, the Zapatista uprising broke out in Chiapas, partly in protest against it. In the United States it was blamed for lost factory jobs, though economists disagree on how many. Under Donald Trump it was renegotiated and replaced in 2020 by the USMCA.
sum: NAFTA, the North American Free Trade Agreement, joined Canada, the United States and Mexico in one of the world's largest free trade areas. It ran from 1 January 1994 until 2020.
